version.changelog: Initial release: Playwright-based FB group scraper with stealth mode and screenshot capture for LLM vision analysis

vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: facebook-group-monitor
Version: 1.0.0

The facebook-group-monitor skill is a legitimate tool for scraping Facebook group posts using Playwright. The Python script (scripts/fb-group-monitor.py) implements standard scraping logic, including session persistence, stealth mode to avoid detection, and screenshot capture for LLM vision analysis. No evidence of data exfiltration, malicious execution, or prompt injection was found; the code's behavior aligns perfectly with its documented purpose.

llm.summary: The skill appears to implement a Playwright-based Facebook group scraper (matching its description) but has mismatches in declared requirements, stores sensitive persistent session data locally, and asks you to expose screenshots to the agent workspace — review before installing or running.

dimensions.detail: The name/description (Facebook group monitor using Playwright + stealth + persistent login) matches the provided scripts and instructions. However the registry metadata declares no dependencies or required binaries while the setup clearly requires Python 3.10+, Playwright, playwright-stealth, and a Chromium install. That mismatch is notable (the skill will not work without those installs).
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md gives concrete commands (login, status, scrape, clean-shots) and explicitly requires a one-time interactive login from the terminal (not from the agent). It also instructs the agent to save screenshots inside the agent workspace so the vision tool can read them. The instructions are relatively scoped to scraping Facebook groups, but they direct creation and storage of persistent browser session data and screenshots which contain sensitive account/content data — the agent will be asked to read those screenshot files for vision processing.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: There is no install spec in the registry, but the included SETUP.md instructs installing Python packages and running 'playwright install chromium' (Playwright will download a Chromium binary). The lack of an install entry in the metadata is inconsistent and means a human must perform the installation. This is not inherently malicious, but it increases risk because required components are heavy (browser binaries) and the package playwright-stealth is a third-party dependency; user should install and inspect dependencies in a controlled environment.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill does not request explicit API keys, but it requires you to perform an interactive Facebook login and stores persistent session data under scripts/.browser-data. Those session cookies provide the script (and anything with filesystem access) full access to the logged-in Facebook account for as long as the session remains valid. The SKILL.md also suggests pointing screenshot output into the agent workspace so the agent's image tool can access them — that intentionally exposes potentially private images to the agent. An optional FBMON_VENV env var is mentioned in setup but not declared in metadata.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: always:false (good). The skill is allowed to be invoked autonomously (normal platform default). Combined with persistent browser session files, autonomous invocation increases blast radius (an automated agent run could use stored credentials to access Facebook content). The skill does not appear to modify other skills or global agent config.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance:
Before installing or running this skill:
- Only use if you trust the skill source. The code will store Facebook session data (cookies) in scripts/.browser-data — anyone or any process with access to that directory could use your logged-in session. Consider running the skill inside an isolated VM or dedicated machine account.
- Perform the one-time login interactively from a terminal on a machine you control; do not let the agent perform interactive login.
- Inspect and control where screenshots and browser-data are written. Avoid pointing --shots-dir at locations containing other sensitive files; the skill recommends placing screenshots in the agent workspace so vision tooling can read them, which intentionally exposes images to the agent.
- Be aware you must manually install Python 3.10+, playwright and playwright-stealth, and execute 'playwright install chromium' — the registry metadata does not declare these requirements (this is a mismatch). Install and audit dependencies in a safe environment.
- If you plan to run automated cron jobs, limit schedule frequency and review logs and .seen-posts.json regularly. Revoke sessions (logout/clear browser-data) when no longer needed.
- If you want stronger guarantees, request the author to provide explicit install metadata, to document exactly what gets stored in .browser-data, and to add an option to store session data in a secure credential store rather than in a local folder.
